Module name: comparator_3bit

Ports:
- input A [2:0] — first 3-bit operand, unsigned
- input B [2:0] — second 3-bit operand, unsigned
- output A_greater — 1 bit, high when A > B
- output A_equal — 1 bit, high when A == B
- output A_less — 1 bit, high when A < B

Clocking/reset: none. The spec states no clock or reset; do not add any.

Timing: purely combinational. Zero latency — outputs settle from A/B with no pipeline stages or registers. Outputs may be declared as `reg` driven by an `always @(*)` block or as continuous assignments; either is acceptable.

Behaviour: treat A and B as unsigned 3-bit integers (range 0–7) and compare their magnitudes. Exactly one of the three outputs is 1 for every input combination; the other two are 0. Encoding is one-hot at all times: A_greater = (A>B), A_equal = (A==B), A_less = (A<B).

Boundary cases called out by the spec:
- Mutual exclusivity is a hard requirement — the three outputs must never be simultaneously high, and must never all be low, for any of the 64 input combinations.
- No other boundary conditions are stated. There is no overflow, no wrap-around, no invalid-input case, and no unknown/high-Z handling requirement; all 8×8 input combinations are legal and fully specified.

Notes for the implementer: cover all input combinations so no latch is inferred (full assignment of all three outputs in every branch, or a default). No sign extension — the operands are unsigned.

Module name: adder_8bit

Ports (all vectors little-endian, [MSB:0]):
- input  a[7:0]   — 8-bit operand A
- input  b[7:0]   — 8-bit operand B
- input  cin      — 1-bit carry-in
- output sum[7:0] — 8-bit sum result
- output cout     — 1-bit carry-out

Clocking/reset: none. The spec states combinational logic only; no clock or reset ports exist.

Timing: purely combinational, zero latency. Outputs settle from inputs with no pipeline stages and no state elements. Outputs must be driven for every input combination (no latches).

Behaviour: The module computes {cout, sum} = a + b + cin as an unsigned 9-bit result. Internally it is built as a ripple chain of eight 1-bit full adders: stage i takes a[i], b[i], and the carry from stage i-1 (stage 0 takes cin), producing sum[i] = a[i] ^ b[i] ^ carry_in_i and carry_out_i = (a[i] & b[i]) | (carry_in_i & (a[i] ^ b[i])). The carry out of stage 7 is cout.

Structure requirement: The spec explicitly calls for "multiple bit-level adders" — implement a separate 1-bit full-adder building block (submodule or repeated instantiation) and chain eight of them, rather than writing a single `a + b + cin` expression.

Boundary cases called out by the spec:
- Overflow beyond 8 bits is captured by cout rather than lost, e.g. a=8'hFF, b=8'h01, cin=0 gives sum=8'h00, cout=1.
- Maximum case a=8'hFF, b=8'hFF, cin=1 gives sum=8'hFF, cout=1.
- cin=1 with a=b=0 gives sum=8'h01, cout=0.
- Only unsigned interpretation is specified; no signed-overflow flag is required.

```
MODULE
  adder_16bit

PORTS
  input  a   [15:0]   operand A
  input  b   [15:0]   operand B
  input  Cin          carry-in, 1 bit
  output y   [15:0]   sum
  output Co           carry-out, 1 bit

TIMING
  Purely combinational. No clock, no reset, no pipeline stages.
  Outputs settle from inputs only; zero-cycle latency.

STRUCTURE (required by spec)
  Define a smaller 8-bit adder module and instantiate it twice inside
  adder_16bit. Low instance handles bits [7:0] with Cin; its carry-out
  feeds the high instance's carry-in for bits [15:8]. The high
  instance's carry-out drives Co. Do not implement the 16-bit sum as a
  single flat expression.

BEHAVIOUR
  {Co, y} = a + b + Cin, computed as a 17-bit unsigned result: y is the
  low 16 bits, Co is bit 16.

BOUNDARY CASES
  Unsigned overflow past 16 bits is reported on Co; y wraps modulo 2^16
  (e.g. a=b=16'hFFFF, Cin=1 gives y=16'hFFFF, Co=1). No other special
  cases are stated in the description.
```

module accu

Ports:
- clk: input, 1 bit
- rst_n: input, 1 bit
- data_in: input, 8 bits [7:0]
- valid_in: input, 1 bit
- valid_out: output reg, 1 bit
- data_out: output reg, 10 bits [9:0]

Clocking/reset:
- All state updates on posedge clk.
- rst_n is active-low, asynchronous reset (posedge clk or negedge rst_n). On reset: data_out = 0, valid_out = 0, internal accumulator = 0, internal counter = 0.

Type: sequential (registered outputs).

Behaviour:
- Maintain a 2-bit (or mod-4) counter of accepted inputs and a 10-bit accumulator. On a clock edge with valid_in==1, add data_in to the accumulator and advance the counter; cycles with valid_in==0 are ignored entirely (counter and accumulator hold).
- On the clock edge that accepts the 4th valid input, data_out is registered with the sum of those four data_in values and valid_out is driven to 1 for exactly that one cycle; the counter and accumulator reset to 0 so the next four valid inputs form an independent group.

Latency: data_out/valid_out appear on the cycle immediately following the 4th valid_in (1 clock after the 4th sample is presented).

Boundary cases stated by the spec:
- Fewer than four accepted inputs: no output event, valid_out stays 0.
- valid_out is high for exactly 1 cycle per completed group, 0 otherwise.
- 4 × 8-bit max (4×255 = 1020) fits in 10 bits, so no overflow handling is required; sum is unsigned.
- Counter wraps 0→1→2→3→0 across successive groups; accumulation is per-group, not cumulative across groups.

Module name: adder_bcd

Ports:
- input  A   [3:0]  — first BCD digit (0–9)
- input  B   [3:0]  — second BCD digit (0–9)
- input  Cin        — 1-bit carry-in
- output Sum [3:0]  — corrected BCD sum digit (0–9)
- output Cout       — 1-bit decimal carry-out

Clocking/reset: none. The spec states no clock or reset, so the module is purely combinational.

Timing: combinational, zero latency. Outputs settle from A, B, Cin only.

Behaviour:
Compute the 5-bit binary sum S = A + B + Cin. If S > 9 (i.e. S exceeds binary 01001, which includes any case where the raw 5-bit sum carries out of bit 3), add 6 (0110) to S and drive Cout = 1; Sum is the low 4 bits of the corrected value. Otherwise Sum = S[3:0] and Cout = 0.

Boundary cases called out by the spec:
- Sum exceeding 9 is the correction trigger: add 6 and assert Cout.
- Maximum legal input case A=9, B=9, Cin=1 gives raw 19, corrected to Sum=9 with Cout=1.
- Sum exactly 9 requires no correction: Sum=9, Cout=0.
- Inputs are stated to be valid BCD (0–9); no behaviour is specified for non-BCD inputs, so none is required.

Module name: comparator_4bit

Ports:
- input A [3:0] — first 4-bit unsigned operand
- input B [3:0] — second 4-bit unsigned operand
- output A_greater — 1 bit, high when A > B
- output A_equal — 1 bit, high when A == B
- output A_less — 1 bit, high when A < B

Clocking/reset: none. The spec states combinational logic only; no clock or reset port exists.

Timing: purely combinational, zero latency. Outputs settle from A and B alone.

Behaviour: Compute the 4-bit subtraction A - B with borrow (equivalently a 5-bit result {borrow, diff} = {1'b0,A} - {1'b0,B}). A_less is the borrow-out of that subtraction. A_equal is high when the 4-bit difference is zero and no borrow occurred. A_greater is high when no borrow occurred and the difference is non-zero. Operands are unsigned.

Boundary cases called out:
- Equality (A == B): difference is zero, no borrow — only A_equal high.
- Borrow-out case (A < B): borrow asserted — only A_less high.
- Mutual exclusivity: exactly one of A_greater, A_equal, A_less is high for every input combination; the three are never simultaneously high and never all low.

No other behaviour is specified — no registered outputs, no enable, no signed comparison, no overflow flag.

Module: adder_32bit

Ports:
- A [32:1], input, 32 bits (MSB is index 32, LSB is index 1)
- B [32:1], input, 32 bits
- S [32:1], output, 32 bits
- C32, output, 1 bit

No clock, no reset. Purely combinational; zero latency.

Behaviour: S and C32 together form the 33-bit unsigned sum A + B with carry-in 0, i.e. {C32, S} = A + B. Carries must be produced by carry-lookahead logic using per-bit generate g = A&B and propagate p = A^B (or A|B), not by a ripple chain.

Structure required by the spec: the top module instantiates a 16-bit CLA block (designed as a separate module) twice — bits [16:1] and bits [32:17]. The lower block takes carry-in 0; its carry-out feeds the upper block's carry-in; the upper block's carry-out is C32.

Boundary cases stated:
- Carry-out of the full 32-bit addition is exposed on C32 (unsigned overflow indicator); it is an output, not discarded.
- All operands are 32-bit; sum bits beyond bit 32 appear only as C32, so the result wraps modulo 2^32 in S.

No signed-overflow flag, no carry-in port, and no other status outputs are specified — do not add them. Port indexing must stay [32:1]/[16:1] style as given, not [31:0].

module div_16bit

Ports:
- A: input, 16 bits, [15:0] — dividend
- B: input, 8 bits, [7:0] — divisor
- result: output reg, 16 bits, [15:0] — quotient
- odd: output reg, 16 bits, [15:0] — remainder

Clock/reset: none. The spec states purely combinational logic; no clock edge, no reset, no pipeline latency (zero-cycle, outputs settle after input change).

Structure: two combinational always blocks, both sensitive to changes on A and B (i.e. always @(*) / always @(A or B)).
- Block 1: loads internal registers a_reg (16-bit) and b_reg (8-bit) from A and B.
- Block 2: performs the restoring-division loop and drives result and odd.

Behaviour: unsigned integer division. Take the top 8 bits of the dividend as the initial partial remainder. At each of the 16 steps, compare the current 8-bit-aligned partial remainder against B: if the remainder is greater than or equal to B, emit quotient bit 1 and replace the remainder with (remainder − B); else emit quotient bit 0 and keep the remainder. Shift the next lower dividend bit into the LSB of the remainder and repeat until all 16 dividend bits are consumed. `result` = the 16 accumulated quotient bits (MSB-first), `odd` = final remainder zero-extended to 16 bits.

Boundary cases: the description calls out none — no divide-by-zero behaviour, no overflow flag, no error output is specified. Do not add any.

Module name: multi_8bit

Ports:
- input  A [7:0]        — multiplicand
- input  B [7:0]        — multiplier
- output product [15:0] — A * B

Clock/reset: none. The spec lists no clock or reset ports, so the module is purely combinational; the shift-and-add loop is unrolled in an always @(*) block (or generate/for loop), not clocked. No pipeline latency — product tracks A and B after combinational delay only.

Behaviour: For each bit i in 0..7 of B, if B[i] is 1, add the multiplicand shifted left by i positions into a 16-bit accumulator; the accumulated sum after all 8 iterations is driven onto product. Equivalent to zero-extending A to 16 bits and summing {16{B[i]}} & (A << i) over i.

Signedness: both operands are unsigned (spec says nothing about sign), so the shifted multiplicand must be zero-extended to 16 bits before accumulating.

Boundary cases:
- Max product 255 * 255 = 65025 fits in 16 bits — no overflow is possible and none is reported.
- A == 0 or B == 0 gives product == 0 (falls out of the accumulate with no special case).
- The shifted multiplicand must be widened to 16 bits before the shift so high-order bits are not lost when i is large (e.g. B[7] set).

No other status/valid/ready flags, no internal state to hold between evaluations.

Module: multi_booth_8bit

Ports:
- clk    : input,  1 bit          — clock
- reset  : input,  1 bit          — reset
- a      : input,  8 bits [7:0]   — value loaded into the `multiplier` register
- b      : input,  8 bits [7:0]   — value loaded into the `multiplicand` register
- p      : output, 16 bits [15:0] — product (register, must hold its value between updates)
- rdy    : output, 1 bit          — register, 1 when multiplication is complete

Clocking / reset: single always block sensitive to `posedge clk or posedge reset` — asynchronous, active-high reset. All outputs are sequential; no combinational outputs.

Internal state (spec-named): `multiplier` 16-bit, `multiplicand` 16-bit, `ctr` 5-bit.

Behaviour:
- Reset (high): multiplier <= {{8{a[7]}}, a}; multiplicand <= {{8{b[7]}}, b}; and initialize p <= 0, rdy <= 0, ctr <= 0.
- Normal operation (reset low): while ctr < 16, each clock edge shift multiplicand left by 1, and if multiplier[ctr] == 1 accumulate p <= p + multiplicand (using the pre-shift or post-shift value consistently — use the value seen by the nonblocking assignment, i.e. p <= p + multiplicand with the unshifted register), then ctr <= ctr + 1.
- When ctr reaches 16, stop updating p/multiplicand/ctr and set rdy <= 1.

Latency: 16 clock cycles after reset deasserts; rdy asserts on the cycle after ctr hits 16 and stays high until the next reset.

Boundary cases stated by the spec: signed operands handled via sign-extension of a and b to 16 bits; ctr is 5 bits so it can represent 16 without wrapping; result truncated/held at 16 bits (no overflow flag).

Module: multi_16bit

Ports:
- clk — input, 1 bit
- rst_n — input, 1 bit
- start — input, 1 bit
- ain — input, 16 bits [15:0] (multiplicand a)
- bin — input, 16 bits [15:0] (multiplier b)
- yout — output, 32 bits [31:0] (product)
- done — output, 1 bit (completion flag)

Clocking/reset: all three registered blocks are `always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n)` — asynchronous, active-low reset (rst_n==0 resets). Fully sequential; no combinational outputs other than the two continuous assignments yout = yout_r, done = done_r.

Internal state (spec-named): i (shift counter, must hold 0..17, so ≥5 bits), areg [15:0], breg [15:0], yout_r [31:0], done_r.

Behaviour:
- Counter: on reset i<=0; else if start && i<17 then i<=i+1; else if !start then i<=0.
- Done: on reset done_r<=0; else if i==16 done_r<=1; else if i==17 done_r<=0.
- Datapath: on reset areg<=0, breg<=0, yout_r<=0; else if start: when i==0 load areg<=ain, breg<=bin (and yout_r<=0 at load); when 0<i<17, if areg[i-1] then yout_r <= yout_r + (breg << (i-1)), i.e. breg shifted left by i-1 with zeros in the low bits; otherwise yout_r holds.

Latency: 17 clocks of start asserted from load (i==0) to done_r rising at i==16; done_r stays high one cycle and clears at i==17. Product valid when done==1.

Boundary cases stated: unsigned 16×16 → 32-bit product cannot overflow; shift amount runs 0..15 only (i-1 for 1≤i≤16); i saturates at 17 while start held, and deasserting start forces i back to 0 (restart). No other edge cases specified.

Module name: multi_pipe_4bit

Parameter:
- size = 4 (module-level parameter, overridable)

Ports:
- clk: input, 1 bit
- rst_n: input, 1 bit
- mul_a: input, [size-1:0] (4 bits), unsigned multiplicand
- mul_b: input, [size-1:0] (4 bits), unsigned multiplier
- mul_out: output reg, [2*size-1:0] (8 bits), unsigned product

Clock/reset:
- All sequential blocks trigger on posedge clk or negedge rst_n (asynchronous, active-low reset).
- On reset: all pipeline registers and mul_out are cleared to 0.

Structure and latency:
- Combinational: zero-extend mul_a and mul_b to 2*size bits; a generate loop for i = 0..size-1 produces partial product temp[i] = mul_b[i] ? (mul_a_extended << i) : {2*size{1'b0}}, each 2*size bits wide.
- Stage 1 (sequential): size/2 = 2 registers, each 2*size bits, hold pairwise sums of adjacent partial products (temp[0]+temp[1], temp[2]+temp[3]).
- Stage 2 (sequential): mul_out registers the sum of the stage-1 registers.
- Total pipeline latency: 2 clock cycles from input presentation to mul_out.

Behaviour: mul_out = mul_a * mul_b (4x4 unsigned) computed as a shift-and-add tree, with results appearing two clocks after the operands are sampled.

Boundary cases stated by the spec: none beyond reset. The 2*size-bit accumulation width holds the maximum product (15*15 = 225) with no overflow; no other special cases are specified.

module multi_pipe_8bit

Ports (all unsigned):
- input  clk
- input  rst_n
- input  mul_en_in
- input  [7:0] mul_a
- input  [7:0] mul_b
- output mul_en_out
- output [15:0] mul_out

Clocking/reset:
- All registers update on posedge clk.
- rst_n is active-low; reset clears mul_en_out_reg, mul_a_reg, mul_b_reg, all sum registers, and mul_out_reg to 0. (Spec does not state sync vs async; either is acceptable — choose one and apply it consistently.)

Sequential/pipeline structure (3 clock stages, latency = 3 cycles from mul_a/mul_b/mul_en_in sampling to valid mul_out):
- Stage 1: sample mul_a -> mul_a_reg, mul_b -> mul_b_reg, gated by mul_en_in (registers hold when mul_en_in is 0).
- Stage 2: combinational partial products temp[i] = mul_b_reg[i] ? {mul_a_reg} shifted left by i : 0 (i = 0..7, each 16 bits); register grouped partial sums into sum[] registers.
- Stage 3: register mul_out_reg = sum of all partial sums.
- mul_en_out_reg is a 3-bit shift register: on each posedge it shifts in mul_en_in; mul_en_out = mul_en_out_reg[2] (its MSB), so the enable pipeline matches the data pipeline depth.

Behaviour:
- Computes the full 16-bit unsigned product mul_a * mul_b via shift-and-add partial products summed through the pipeline; new operands may be accepted every cycle while mul_en_in is high.
- Output assignment is combinational from the last stage: mul_out = mul_en_out ? mul_out_reg : 16'b0.

Boundary cases stated by the spec:
- 8x8 unsigned product always fits in 16 bits, so no overflow handling is required.
- mul_out must be forced to 0 whenever mul_en_out is inactive.
- Input registers must not update while mul_en_in is inactive.

MODULE: fixed_point_subtractor

PARAMETERS
  Q — number of fractional bits (no default given; use Q=15)
  N — total bit width of operands/result (no default given; use N=32)

PORTS
  input  [N-1:0] a   — first fixed-point operand
  input  [N-1:0] b   — second fixed-point operand
  output [N-1:0] c   — subtraction result, a - b

CLOCK/RESET: none. The spec names no clock or reset port.

TIMING: purely combinational. Zero latency, no pipeline stages. `res [N-1:0]` is an internal
`reg` driven by an always @(*) block; `c` is a continuous assignment from `res`.

NUMBER FORMAT: sign-magnitude. Bit [N-1] is the sign (0 = positive, 1 = negative);
bits [N-2:0] are the magnitude, of which the low Q bits are fractional and the
upper N-1-Q bits are integer. Magnitudes are compared/combined as one unsigned field.

BEHAVIOUR
  Same sign (a[N-1] == b[N-1]): subtract the smaller magnitude from the larger;
  result sign = a's sign if |a| >= |b|, else the inverted sign.
  Different sign: add the two magnitudes; result sign = a[N-1] (the sign of a is kept).

BOUNDARY CASES
  Zero result: if the magnitude field res[N-2:0] is all zeros, force res[N-1] = 0
  so that negative zero is never produced.
  No overflow/saturation behaviour is specified; magnitude carry out of bit N-2 is not handled.

MODULE
  fixed_point_adder

PARAMETERS
  Q — number of fractional bits; N — total bits (sign + integer + fractional). Both are module parameters with implementer-chosen defaults (spec gives none). Q is not used in any datapath expression here — alignment is implicit since both operands and the result share the same Q.

PORTS
  input  [N-1:0] a   — operand 1, sign-magnitude: a[N-1] = sign, a[N-2:0] = magnitude
  input  [N-1:0] b   — operand 2, same format
  output [N-1:0] c   — result, same format

TIMING
  Purely combinational. No clock, no reset, no pipeline stages — the spec names no clock or reset port. `res [N-1:0]` is an internal variable assigned in a combinational always block (declared reg), driving c continuously; c must equal res with zero latency.

BEHAVIOUR
  Same signs (a[N-1] == b[N-1]): res[N-2:0] = a[N-2:0] + b[N-2:0]; res[N-1] = a[N-1].
  Different signs: compare magnitudes a[N-2:0] vs b[N-2:0]. If a's magnitude > b's: res[N-2:0] = a[N-2:0] - b[N-2:0], res[N-1] = 0. If b's magnitude > a's: res[N-2:0] = b[N-2:0] - a[N-2:0], res[N-1] = 1 unless the difference is zero, in which case res[N-1] = 0. Equal magnitudes with opposite signs must yield all-zero c (+0, never -0).

BOUNDARY CASES
  Overflow: magnitude sum may exceed N-1 bits; the carry out of bit N-2 is not propagated into the sign bit — the sign bit is written from the operand sign only, so the magnitude wraps within N-1 bits. No overflow flag port exists.
  Zero result on the subtract path must be emitted with sign 0.

# Interface Contract — sub_64bit

Module name: sub_64bit

Ports:
- input  A      [63:0]  — first operand (signed, two's complement)
- input  B      [63:0]  — second operand (signed, two's complement), subtrahend
- output result [63:0]  — A - B
- output overflow       — 1 bit, signed-overflow flag

Clocking/reset: none. The spec states no clock or reset signals; do not add any.

Timing: purely combinational, zero latency. Outputs must settle from A and B alone (continuous assignment or always @(*) with reg-typed outputs).

Behaviour:
- result = A - B computed as 64-bit two's-complement subtraction; the difference wraps modulo 2^64 (carry/borrow out of bit 63 is discarded, and result must remain a truthful 64-bit low-order difference even when overflow is flagged).
- overflow = 1 exactly when the signed result cannot be represented in 64 bits, determined from sign bits A[63], B[63], result[63]:
  - positive overflow: A[63]==0 && B[63]==1 && result[63]==1
  - negative overflow: A[63]==1 && B[63]==0 && result[63]==0
  - overflow = 0 in all other cases, including whenever A[63]==B[63].

Boundary cases called out by the spec:
- Overflow only when operand signs differ; same-sign subtraction never overflows.
- Wrap-around of `result` on overflow is retained, not saturated or zeroed.
- No divide-by-zero, full/empty, or unsigned-borrow conditions apply to this module.

Module name: JC_counter

Ports:
- clk — input, 1 bit
- rst_n — input, 1 bit
- Q — output reg, 64 bits, [63:0]

Clocking/reset:
- Sequential logic only. Single always block sensitive to posedge clk and negedge rst_n (asynchronous, active-low reset).
- Reset action: Q <= 64'b0.

Behaviour (per clock, when not in reset):
- If Q[0] == 0: Q <= {1'b1, Q[63:1]} — right-shift, insert 1 at MSB.
- If Q[0] == 1: Q <= {1'b0, Q[63:1]} — right-shift, insert 0 at MSB.
- No other state, no pipeline latency: Q updates on the clock edge and is the register output directly.

State sequence (wrap-around):
- Starting from all zeros, fills with 1s from the MSB downward over 64 cycles (0000…0 → 1000…0 → 1100…0 → … → 111…1), then empties 1s from the MSB downward over the next 64 cycles (011…1 → 001…1 → … → 000…1 → 000…0), giving a 128-state cycle that returns to 0 automatically. No overflow, error, enable, or load conditions are specified.

Module: counter_12

Ports:
- input  clk         : 1-bit, clock
- input  rst_n       : 1-bit, active-low reset
- input  valid_count : 1-bit, count enable
- output out         : 4-bit, [3:0], registered (reg)

Timing:
- Sequential logic, single always block on posedge clk.
- Reset is asynchronous active-low (negedge rst_n in sensitivity list); out <= 4'b0000 while rst_n is low.
- No pipeline latency: out updates on the clock edge, so a new value is visible one cycle after the enabling condition.

Behaviour:
- Reset has priority over counting.
- When rst_n is high and valid_count is 1: if out == 4'd11, out <= 4'b0000, else out <= out + 1'b1.
- When valid_count is 0, out holds its current value.

Boundary cases called out:
- Wrap-around at terminal count 4'd11 back to 4'b0000 (count sequence is 0..11, modulo 12); the counter never reaches 12–15.
- Hold/pause when valid_count is deasserted — no increment, no loss of state.
- Reset asserted at any time forces 4'b0000 regardless of valid_count.

Module name: up_down_counter

Ports (all synchronous to `clk`):
- clk — input, 1-bit — clock; all state updates on rising edge (posedge clk)
- reset — input, 1-bit — active-high, synchronous reset; when asserted, count is cleared to 16'd0 (takes priority over up_down)
- up_down — input, 1-bit — direction control: 1 = increment, 0 = decrement
- count — output, 16-bit, [15:0] — registered current counter value

Type: sequential only. No combinational outputs, no pipeline latency beyond the single register — a change on up_down affects `count` at the next rising edge.

Behaviour: On each posedge clk, if reset is high, count <= 16'd0; else if up_down is high, count <= count + 1; else count <= count - 1. `count` is the register itself, so it is always the current stored value (0 to 65535).

Boundary cases stated by the spec:
- count range is 0 to 65535 (full 16-bit unsigned range); arithmetic is 16-bit modulo-65536, so incrementing at 65535 wraps to 0 and decrementing at 0 wraps to 65535. The spec names no saturation or overflow flag — do not add one.
- reset dominates both counting directions.

ring_counter — interface contract

Module name: ring_counter

Ports:
- clk : input, 1 bit — clock
- reset : input, 1 bit — reset
- out : output, 8 bits, range [7:0] — registered (declared as reg / driven from the sequential block)

Clocking / reset:
- Sequential logic, all state updates on the rising edge of clk (posedge clk).
- reset is active-high. The spec states only "when reset is high"; implement it as synchronous (evaluated inside the posedge clk block). Asynchronous reset (posedge reset in the sensitivity list) is an acceptable alternative but is not required by the text — pick one and be consistent.
- No pipeline latency: out changes one clock edge after the shift condition, i.e. out is the current state itself.

Behaviour:
- out is a one-hot 8-bit value: exactly one bit is 1 at all times. On each rising clk edge with reset low, the set bit moves one position toward the MSB (out <= {out[6:0], out[7]}), i.e. 0000_0001 → 0000_0010 → ... → 1000_0000 → 0000_0001.
- When reset is high, out is loaded with 8'b0000_0001 (LSB set), which is also the state the sequence starts from.

Boundary cases called out:
- Wrap-around: after out = 8'b1000_0000 (MSB set), the next state returns to 8'b0000_0001 (LSB set); the rotation is closed, so no bit is ever lost and no all-zero state occurs.
- Reset dominates the shift: if reset is high at a clock edge, the state is 8'b0000_0001 regardless of the previous value.
- No overflow, divide-by-zero, or full/empty conditions apply to this design.

MODULE CONTRACT — module name: `fsm`

PORTS
- IN    : input,  1 bit — serial data bit, sampled per clock
- CLK   : input,  1 bit — clock
- RST   : input,  1 bit — reset
- MATCH : output, 1 bit — sequence-detected flag (declare as `reg`/always-driven)

CLOCKING / RESET
- State register updates on posedge CLK.
- RST is active-high and asynchronous (spec lists RST alongside posedge CLK in the sensitivity list); when RST is asserted, MATCH is forced to 0 and the FSM returns to its idle/start state.

STRUCTURE
- Mealy FSM: sequential next-state register + combinational output.
- MATCH is a combinational function of (current state, current IN) — no output register, no extra pipeline latency. It must assert in the same cycle in which the final `1` of the pattern is present on IN, i.e. concurrent with the 5th bit, not one cycle later.
- 5 states are sufficient (idle + "1" + "10" + "100" + "1001" seen).

BEHAVIOUR
Detect the bit pattern 10011 arriving MSB-first, one bit per clock, on IN. MATCH = 1 exactly when the FSM is in the "1001 already seen" state and IN = 1 at that moment; MATCH = 0 in every other state/input combination.

BOUNDARY CASES CALLED OUT
- Continuous/streaming input: the detector never stops — it keeps scanning after a match.
- Overlapping (loop) detection: the final `1` of a completed match is reused as the first `1` of the next candidate. For the stream 1,0,0,1,1,0,0,1,1 MATCH must pulse on bit 5 and again on bit 9.
- Partial-match backtracking: on a mismatch the next state must fall back to the longest valid prefix of 10011 that the just-received bit still satisfies (e.g. a `1` mid-sequence restarts the prefix as "1" rather than dropping to idle), not unconditionally to idle.
- Reset dominates: MATCH = 0 while RST is asserted regardless of IN or state.

Module name: adder_pipe_64bit

Ports:
- clk — input, 1 bit
- rst_n — input, 1 bit
- i_en — input, 1 bit
- adda — input, 64 bits [63:0]
- addb — input, 64 bits [63:0]
- result — output, 65 bits [64:0], registered
- o_en — output, 1 bit, registered

Clocking/reset: all state updates on posedge clk; reset is active-low (rst_n) — asynchronous (`always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n)`) with all pipeline registers, result, and o_en cleared to 0 on reset.

Type: fully sequential (pipelined). Design as a ripple-carry adder split into N equal pipeline stages across the 64 bits; use 4 stages of 16 bits each. Fixed latency = 4 clock cycles from the cycle in which i_en is sampled to the cycle in which result/o_en are valid. Throughput one addition per cycle; a new operand pair may be accepted every cycle.

Behaviour: on each posedge clk, operands adda/addb are captured and the low 16-bit slice is summed; each later stage adds its 16-bit slice plus the carry-out registered from the previous stage, while the already-computed lower sum bits and the not-yet-consumed upper operand bits are shifted forward through pipeline registers. After the final stage, result = {carry_out_of_bit63, sum[63:0]}, i.e. the full 65-bit unsigned sum of adda + addb.

Enable path: i_en is registered through a shift chain of the same depth as the datapath (4 stages); o_en is the last element of that chain, so o_en = 1 exactly on the cycle that result holds the sum for the operands accepted 4 cycles earlier. When i_en = 0 the corresponding pipeline slot produces o_en = 0; datapath registers may still shift (their result is simply not flagged valid).

Boundary cases: result is 65 bits wide so the carry out of bit 63 is captured in result[64] — no overflow is possible or flagged. All arithmetic is unsigned. No other boundary conditions are specified.

Module name: LIFObuffer

Ports:
- input Clk
- input Rst
- input EN
- input RW
- input [3:0] dataIn
- output EMPTY
- output FULL
- output [3:0] dataOut

Clocking/reset:
- All state updates on the rising edge of Clk, gated by EN (nothing changes when EN is low).
- Rst is active high and synchronous — it is evaluated inside the EN-gated clocked block, so reset only takes effect when EN is high.

Sequential vs combinational:
- Fully sequential; dataOut, EMPTY, FULL, SP and stack_mem are all registers updated in the clocked block. No pipeline stages beyond the single register update: a pop's data appears on dataOut one clock after the pop is issued.

State/behaviour:
- Internal state: stack_mem, 4 entries of 4 bits, indexed by a 3-bit stack pointer SP that counts down from 4 (empty) to 0 (full).
- On Rst: SP <= 4, all four stack_mem entries <= 0, buffer returns to empty.
- Otherwise, with EN high: if RW==0 and not FULL, write dataIn into stack_mem at the location addressed by the decremented pointer and decrement SP (push). If RW==1 and not EMPTY, read the entry at the current SP location into dataOut, clear that entry to 0, and increment SP (pop).

Boundary cases called out:
- FULL is asserted when SP reaches 0; a write while FULL is ignored (no data stored, SP unchanged).
- EMPTY is asserted when SP equals 4; a read while EMPTY is ignored (dataOut unchanged, SP unchanged).
- SP never wraps past 0 or 4; the flags are recomputed from SP after each operation.

Module: right_shifter

Ports:
- clk : input, 1 bit — clock
- d : input, 1 bit — serial input bit
- q : output, 8 bits [7:0] — shift register contents, must be declared as `reg [7:0] q`

Clocking/reset:
- Sequential logic, single always block triggered on posedge clk.
- No reset port. q is initialized to 8'b0 via an `initial` statement only.

Behaviour:
- On each rising clk edge, q takes the value {d, q[7:1]}: existing contents shift right one position (q[0] discarded), and d is loaded into the MSB q[7].
- Use non-blocking assignments; the spec expresses this as `q <= (q >> 1)` together with `q[7] <= d`, which must resolve to MSB = d, not 0.

Latency: the input bit d appears at q[7] one clock cycle after it is presented; a given bit reaches q[0] after 8 clock cycles and is then discarded.

Boundary cases: none specified — no overflow, no wrap-around, no reset condition. Bit shifted out of q[0] is simply lost.

Module name: sequence_detector

Ports (all 1-bit scalars):
- input clk — clock
- input reset_n — reset, active-low (name implies negated polarity)
- input data_in — serial bitstream, one bit per clock
- output sequence_detected — detection flag

Clocking/reset:
- All state updates on posedge clk.
- Reset returns the FSM to IDLE. Spec text says "when reset is high" but the port is named reset_n; treat it as active-low (reset_n == 0 → IDLE) since the port name is the normative signal. Implement it as asynchronous (`always @(posedge clk or negedge reset_n)`) — synchronous is acceptable if the testbench only deasserts reset before the first active edge.

Structure:
- Sequential FSM with states IDLE, S1, S2, S3, S4 registered on clk.
- Latency: sequence_detected asserts in the same clock cycle in which the FSM enters S4, i.e. one clock after the final '1' of the pattern is sampled. Register the output with the state (no combinational glitch path from data_in).

Behaviour:
- Detect the bit pattern 1001 arriving MSB-first on data_in, one bit per rising clk edge: '1' → S1, '0' → S2, '0' → S3, '1' → S4.
- sequence_detected is high only while in S4 and low in every other state (single-cycle pulse per detection).

Boundary cases stated by the spec:
- Reset asserted at any time forces IDLE and clears sequence_detected, aborting a partial match.
- On a mismatch mid-sequence, fall back to the longest still-valid prefix rather than always to IDLE: from S1 a '0' advances to S2 and a '1' stays in S1; from S2 a '0' advances to S3 and a '1' returns to S1; from S3 a '1' advances to S4 and a '0' returns to IDLE.
- Overlapping detections: the spec does not state whether the trailing '1' of one match may start the next. From S4, treat it as the first bit already seen — '1' → S1, '0' → IDLE — so 1001001 reports one detection, not two. (Non-overlapping restart from S4 would be the alternative; this contract picks overlap-free-per-bit reuse of the trailing '1'.)
- No other exceptional conditions (no overflow, full/empty, or wrap-around) are described.

Module name: freq_div

Ports (all 1-bit scalars):
- input CLK_in — 100 MHz reference clock
- input RST — reset
- output reg CLK_50 — CLK_in / 2 (50 MHz)
- output reg CLK_10 — CLK_in / 10 (10 MHz)
- output reg CLK_1 — CLK_in / 100 (1 MHz)

Clocking/reset: three separate always blocks, each sensitive to posedge CLK_in or posedge RST — i.e. asynchronous, active-high reset. All outputs are sequential registers; no combinational outputs, no pipeline latency requirement.

Internal state (not ports): cnt_10 and cnt_100, unsigned counters. cnt_10 must hold 0..4 (≥3 bits), cnt_100 must hold 0..49 (≥6 bits). Both reset to 0 on RST.

Behaviour:
- CLK_50: on each posedge CLK_in, CLK_50 <= ~CLK_50; RST forces CLK_50 to 0.
- CLK_10: cnt_10 increments each posedge CLK_in; when cnt_10 == 4, toggle CLK_10 and clear cnt_10 to 0 (5-cycle half period → divide-by-10). RST forces CLK_10 = 0 and cnt_10 = 0.
- CLK_1: cnt_100 increments each posedge CLK_in; when cnt_100 == 49, toggle CLK_1 and clear cnt_100 to 0 (50-cycle half period → divide-by-100). RST forces CLK_1 = 0 and cnt_100 = 0.

Boundary cases stated by the spec:
- Counter terminal values are exactly 4 and 49; on reaching them the counter wraps to 0 in the same cycle as the toggle (no count to 5 or 50).
- Asynchronous reset takes priority over counting and toggling; all three outputs and both counters go to 0 immediately.
- No other cases (overflow, enable, division error) are specified.
INTERFACE CONTRACT — LFSR

module float_multi

Ports (all single module, no parameters):
- clk        : input, 1 bit
- rst        : input, 1 bit
- a          : input, 32 bits [31:0]
- b          : input, 32 bits [31:0]
- z          : output reg, 32 bits [31:0]

Clocking/reset:
- Single always block on posedge clk.
- rst is active high; treat as synchronous (spec only says "counter is reset to zero on rst"). On reset, counter <= 0.

Structure: fully sequential, multi-cycle FSM driven by counter [2:0]. No fixed pipeline latency is stated; the sequence is one operation at a time, stepping counter 0..7 and wrapping back to 0 to begin the next multiply. z is registered and only updated in the final output cycle.

Required internal state (names fixed by the spec):
counter [2:0]; a_mantissa/b_mantissa/z_mantissa [23:0]; a_exponent/b_exponent/z_exponent [9:0] (signed-biased, wide enough for over/underflow detection); a_sign/b_sign/z_sign; product [49:0]; guard_bit, round_bit, sticky.

Behaviour: unpack a and b into sign, 8-bit exponent, and 24-bit mantissa (implicit leading 1 for normal numbers, leading 0 for subnormals); handle special cases; normalize subnormal operands; compute product = a_mantissa * b_mantissa and z_exponent = a_exponent + b_exponent - 127 (bias removed once), z_sign = a_sign ^ b_sign; normalize the 50-bit product (shift left while MSB region is unnormalized, or right by 1 and increment exponent when the product is 2.0 or greater), extract guard/round/sticky from the discarded low bits, apply round-to-nearest-even, renormalize if rounding overflows the mantissa, then pack sign/exponent/mantissa into z.

Boundary cases called out by the spec:
- NaN in: if either operand is NaN, output NaN. Also 0 x infinity produces NaN.
- Infinity in: infinity times any nonzero finite gives infinity with the XOR sign.
- Zero operand: result is signed zero.
- Overflow: exponent above the max representable -> signed infinity.
- Underflow: exponent below the minimum -> signed zero (subnormal handling on the output is not required by the description beyond this).

Module: edge_detect

Ports:
- clk: input, 1-bit — clock
- rst_n: input, 1-bit — active-low reset
- a: input, 1-bit — signal to monitor
- rise: output reg, 1-bit
- down: output reg, 1-bit

Clocking/reset:
- All state updates on posedge clk. Reset is active-low (rst_n == 0); spec does not state synchronicity — implement as asynchronous negedge rst_n (`always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n)`), which is the conventional reading of "active low reset" here. On reset: rise = 0, down = 0, and the stored previous-a register = 0.

Sequential/latency:
- Fully sequential, no combinational outputs. Latency: 1 clock cycle from the sampled edge of `a` to the corresponding output pulse.

Behaviour:
- Register the previous sampled value of `a` (call it a_d) every clock. On each posedge clk, rise <= (~a_d & a) and down <= (a_d & ~a); both are 0 in every other cycle. Outputs are therefore one-cycle-wide pulses appearing the clock after the transition is captured, returning to 0 automatically until the next matching edge.

Boundary cases stated:
- `a` is slowly changing, so no adjacent-edge/back-to-back transition case is required.
- rise and down are mutually exclusive; never both 1 in the same cycle.
- After reset (a_d = 0), if `a` is already 1 at the first clock, that counts as a rising edge and rise pulses once.
- No overflow, division, FIFO full/empty, or wrap-around conditions in this spec.

Module name: calendar

Ports (all 1-bit unless noted):
- CLK — input, clock
- RST — input, active-high reset
- Hours — output reg [5:0]
- Mins — output reg [5:0]
- Secs — output reg [5:0]

Clocking/reset:
- Three separate always blocks, each `posedge CLK or posedge RST` (asynchronous, active-high reset). Reset forces Hours=Mins=Secs=0.
- Purely sequential; no pipeline latency — outputs are the register values themselves.

Behaviour:
- Secs increments every clock, wrapping 59→0.
- Mins increments on the clock where Secs==59, wrapping 59→0 when Mins==59 && Secs==59.
- Hours increments on the clock where Mins==59 && Secs==59, wrapping 23→0 when Hours==23 && Mins==59 && Secs==59.
- All three registers hold their value otherwise; all comparisons use the current (pre-update) values so the carry cascade happens in the same cycle.

Boundary cases called out:
- Secs wrap 59→0; Mins wrap 59→0 at Secs==59; Hours wrap 23→0 at 23:59:59.
- Reset from any state returns to 00:00:00 immediately (async).
- Initial/starting value after reset is 0 for all three counters.

MODULE: parallel2serial

PORTS
  clk        input   1-bit    clock
  rst_n      input   1-bit    active-low reset
  d          input   4-bit    [3:0] parallel data in
  valid_out  output  1-bit    registered
  dout       output  1-bit    serial data out

CLOCK/RESET
  All state updates on posedge clk. Reset is active-low (rst_n==0), asynchronous
  (always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n)); on reset clear cnt, data, and valid to 0.

STRUCTURE
  Sequential core: 2-bit counter cnt, 4-bit shift register data, 1-bit valid register.
  dout is a combinational tap on the register: dout = data[3] (MSB of data).
  valid_out = valid register. No extra pipeline stages beyond these registers.

BEHAVIOUR
  Each clock: if cnt == 3, load data <= d, cnt <= 0, valid <= 1; otherwise
  cnt <= cnt + 1, valid <= 0, and data <= {data[2:0], data[3]} (left-rotate by one,
  MSB wrapped into the LSB).
  So a new 4-bit word is captured every 4th cycle, and its bits appear on dout MSB-first
  over the next 4 cycles; valid_out is high only on the cycle where the MSB is presented.

BOUNDARY CASES
  cnt wraps 0->1->2->3->0 (2-bit counter, no overflow beyond modulo-4).
  data shift is a rotation, not a zero-fill: bit shifted out of the MSB re-enters the LSB.
  No overflow, divide-by-zero, or full/empty conditions in this spec.

Module: asyn_fifo
Parameters: WIDTH = 8, DEPTH = 16
Submodule (must be instantiated): dual_port_RAM, parameters WIDTH/DEPTH, ports wclk, wenc, waddr[$clog2(DEPTH)-1:0], wdata[WIDTH-1:0], rclk, renc, raddr[$clog2(DEPTH)-1:0], rdata (output reg [WIDTH-1:0]).

Ports of asyn_fifo:
  input  wclk, rclk            1 bit each
  input  wrstn, rrstn          1 bit each, active-low
  input  winc, rinc            1 bit each
  input  [WIDTH-1:0] wdata
  output wfull, rempty         1 bit each
  output [WIDTH-1:0] rdata

Clocking/reset: all write-domain state on posedge wclk with asynchronous active-low wrstn; all read-domain state on posedge rclk with asynchronous active-low rrstn. Fully sequential; rdata is the registered RAM output, so read data appears one rclk after the accepted read (rinc & ~rempty).

Behaviour: binary pointers waddr_bin/raddr_bin are $clog2(DEPTH)+1 bits wide and increment by 1 on an accepted write (winc & ~wfull) / accepted read (rinc & ~rempty). Each binary pointer is converted to Gray (bin ^ (bin>>1)) into wptr/rptr. wptr crosses into the read domain through two rclk flops (wptr_buff → wptr_syn); rptr crosses into the write domain through two wclk flops (rptr_buff → rptr_syn). The low $clog2(DEPTH) bits of the binary pointers drive waddr/raddr; wenc = winc & ~wfull, renc = rinc & ~rempty.

Boundary cases:
  rempty = (rptr == wptr_syn) — Gray pointers equal in the read domain.
  wfull  = (wptr == {~rptr_syn[MSB], ~rptr_syn[MSB-1], rptr_syn[MSB-2:0]}) — top two Gray bits inverted, remaining bits equal, i.e. write pointer has wrapped exactly DEPTH ahead.
  No write when wfull, no read when rempty; pointers wrap naturally at 2*DEPTH.
  Reset drives waddr_bin/raddr_bin, wptr/rptr, and both synchronizer stages to 0, so rempty is 1 and wfull is 0 out of reset.

Module name: synchronizer

Ports:
- clk_a — input, 1 bit
- clk_b — input, 1 bit
- arstn — input, 1 bit
- brstn — input, 1 bit
- data_in — input, 4 bits [3:0]
- data_en — input, 1 bit
- dataout — output, 4 bits [3:0] (registered, needs reg type)

Clocking / reset:
- clk_a domain: posedge clk_a, asynchronous active-low arstn (`always @(posedge clk_a or negedge arstn)`).
- clk_b domain: posedge clk_b, asynchronous active-low brstn (`always @(posedge clk_b or negedge brstn)`).
- All logic is sequential; no combinational outputs.

Behaviour:
- clk_a domain: data_reg <= data_in; en_data_reg <= data_en. Both reset to 0 on arstn low.
- clk_b domain: en_clap_one <= en_data_reg; en_clap_two <= en_clap_one (two-flop enable synchronizer). Both reset to 0 on brstn low.
- clk_b domain output: on brstn low dataout <= 4'b0; else if en_clap_two is high dataout <= data_reg; else dataout holds its previous value.

Latency: enable path is 1 clk_a cycle plus 2 clk_b cycles; dataout updates on the clk_b edge after en_clap_two is high, so total is 3 clk_b cycles of enable latency on top of the clk_a capture.

Boundary cases stated by the spec: data_in is stable while data_en is high; data_en asserted for ≥3 clk_b cycles; ≥10 clk_b cycles between data changes — so no metastability handling beyond the two-flop enable chain and no handshake/ack is required. data_reg is intentionally not synchronized into clk_b (MUX-based scheme relies on the enable delay). dataout holds last value when en_clap_two is low.

Module: freq_divbyodd

Parameter:
- NUM_DIV, integer, default 5 (odd divisor)

Ports:
- input  clk        — 1 bit, source clock
- input  rst_n      — 1 bit, active-low reset
- output clk_div    — 1 bit, divided clock (may be `wire`, driven combinationally from the two internal dividers)

Clocking/reset:
- cnt1 and clk_div1 are sequential on posedge clk; cnt2 and clk_div2 are sequential on negedge clk.
- rst_n is asynchronous active-low on both domains (`always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n)` / `always @(negedge clk or negedge rst_n)`); reset clears both counters to 0 and both clk_div1/clk_div2 to 0.

Sequential vs combinational:
- Counters and the two half-phase divider flops are sequential; clk_div is purely combinational: clk_div = clk_div1 | clk_div2. No pipeline latency requirement.

Behaviour:
- cnt1 increments on each rising edge, cnt2 on each falling edge; each wraps from NUM_DIV-1 back to 0 (modulo NUM_DIV).
- clk_div1 toggles when cnt1 reaches (NUM_DIV-1)/2 and when cnt1 reaches NUM_DIV-1; clk_div2 toggles identically off cnt2 on the falling edge. OR-ing the two half-cycle-offset waveforms yields clk_div with period NUM_DIV*clk and 50% duty.

Boundary cases stated by the spec:
- NUM_DIV is assumed odd; the counters wrap at NUM_DIV-1 (no overflow beyond the count range).
- rst_n asserted low forces cnt1, cnt2, clk_div1, clk_div2 to 0, hence clk_div = 0.
- No other error/edge conditions (no divide-by-zero, full/empty, or overflow flags) are specified.

Module: barrel_shifter (plus submodule mux2X1)

Ports (barrel_shifter):
- in [7:0], input — 8-bit data to shift
- ctrl [2:0], input — shift amount control (one-hot-per-stage: bit2=4, bit1=2, bit0=1)
- out [7:0], output — 8-bit shifted result

Submodule mux2X1:
- in0, input, 1 bit — selected when sel=0
- in1, input, 1 bit — selected when sel=1
- sel, input, 1 bit
- out, output, 1 bit

Clocking/reset: none. No clock or reset ports; the spec implies no sequential elements.

Timing: purely combinational, zero latency. `out` responds immediately to `in`/`ctrl`.

Behaviour: three cascaded mux stages. Stage 1 selects between `in` and `in` shifted by 4 under ctrl[2]; stage 2 selects between stage-1 output and that output shifted by 2 under ctrl[1]; stage 3 selects between stage-2 output and that output shifted by 1 under ctrl[0]. Every bit of every stage is produced by a mux2X1 instance. Net effect: shift by ctrl[2]*4 + ctrl[1]*2 + ctrl[0]*1 positions, i.e. 0 to 7.

Boundary cases stated by the spec: ctrl = 3'b000 passes `in` through unchanged; ctrl = 3'b111 gives the maximum shift of 7. The spec's title says "rotating bits" while the implementation text says only "shifted" — implement each stage as a left rotate (bits leaving the top re-enter at the bottom), so no bits are lost and no zero-fill is needed; state this assumption in a comment.

**Module:** `traffic_light`

**Ports**
- `input clk` — 1 bit
- `input rst_n` — 1 bit
- `input pass_request` — 1 bit
- `output [7:0] clock` — 8 bit, continuous assign of internal `cnt`
- `output reg red, yellow, green` — 1 bit each, registered

**Clocking/reset:** all sequential blocks trigger on `posedge clk or negedge rst_n`; reset is active-low and asynchronous.

**Sequential/comb split:** three sequential always blocks (state+next-output logic, counter, output register) plus one continuous assign for `clock`. Outputs `red/yellow/green` lag their next-value registers `p_red/p_yellow/p_green` by one clock — 1-cycle output latency.

**State:** 2-bit `state` over parameters `idle`, `s1_red`, `s2_yellow`, `s3_green`. On reset → `idle`, which immediately (next clock) goes to `s1_red` with all lights 0. `s1_red` asserts `p_red` and, when `cnt == 3`, moves to `s3_green`. `s3_green` asserts `p_green` and, when `cnt == 3`, moves to `s2_yellow`. `s2_yellow` asserts `p_yellow` and, when `cnt == 3`, moves back to `s1_red`. Cycle order is red → green → yellow → red.

**Counter (`cnt`, 8-bit, counts down):** reset value 10. Priority of reload conditions each clock: (1) `!rst_n` → 10; (2) `pass_request && green` → 10; (3) `!green && p_green` → 60; (4) `!yellow && p_yellow` → 5; (5) `!red && p_red` → 10; else `cnt <= cnt - 1`. Durations are therefore green 60, yellow 5, red 10 clocks, each loaded one cycle before the corresponding output light goes high.

**Boundary cases stated by the spec:**
- Pedestrian request during green forces `cnt` to 10; if the remaining green count is already ≤ 10 the reload is not an extension (spec says such cases stay unchanged) — the unconditional load to 10 is what the recommended design does, so implement the stated reload.
- No overflow/underflow handling is specified; `cnt` is reloaded before reaching 0 via the `cnt == 3` transition.
- `pass_request` is ignored outside the green state.

Module: width_8to16

Ports:
- clk — input, 1 bit
- rst_n — input, 1 bit
- valid_in — input, 1 bit
- data_in — input, 8 bits [7:0]
- valid_out — output reg, 1 bit
- data_out — output reg, 16 bits [15:0]

Clocking/reset: all state updates on posedge clk; asynchronous active-low reset (negedge rst_n). On reset, data_out <= 16'b0, valid_out <= 1'b0, and the internal capture flag clears.

Type: sequential. Latency: valid_out/data_out assert on the clock cycle immediately following the second valid_in beat (registered outputs, 1-cycle latency measured from that second beat).

Internal state (not ports): data_lock — 8-bit register holding the first captured byte; flag — 1-bit toggle marking that a first byte is pending.

Behaviour: valid_in beats are paired in arrival order. On a beat with flag==0, data_in is stored into data_lock, flag is set, and no output is produced. On a beat with flag==1, data_out is registered as {data_lock, data_in} — first-arrived byte in the high 8 bits [15:8], second in the low 8 bits [7:0] — valid_out is registered high for exactly that one cycle, and flag clears. Cycles with valid_in==0 hold all state unchanged and do not stall or discard the pending byte; a single unpaired byte simply waits indefinitely for the next valid_in.

Boundary cases stated by the spec: an odd/unpaired input byte produces no output until its partner arrives; valid_out is never asserted on the first byte of a pair; reset clears data_out to 0. No overflow, backpressure, or full/empty conditions are specified.

Module name: freq_diveven

Parameter:
- NUM_DIV — integer parameter, division factor, must be even. (Spec gives no default; choose a sensible even default such as 4.)

Ports:
- input clk — 1 bit, clock to be divided
- input rst_n — 1 bit, active-low reset
- output reg clk_div — 1 bit, divided clock output

Clocking/reset:
- All state updates on posedge clk.
- Asynchronous active-low reset on rst_n (negedge rst_n in sensitivity list): clears cnt to 0 and clk_div to 0.

Internal state:
- cnt — 4-bit register (`reg [3:0] cnt`), counts input clock cycles.

Sequential/combinational:
- Fully sequential; no combinational outputs, no pipeline latency requirement.

Behaviour:
- On each posedge clk, if cnt < (NUM_DIV/2 - 1), cnt increments and clk_div holds its value; otherwise cnt resets to 0 and clk_div toggles. This yields an output clock of period NUM_DIV input cycles with 50% duty cycle.

Boundary cases stated by the spec:
- NUM_DIV must be even (odd values are out of scope; no handling required).
- Counter wraps to 0 exactly at the half-period limit rather than free-running.
- Reset forces cnt = 0 and clk_div = 0.
- cnt is fixed at 4 bits, so NUM_DIV/2-1 must fit in 4 bits (NUM_DIV ≤ 32); no overflow handling beyond the wrap above.

Module: RAM

Parameters: WIDTH = 6 (data width), DEPTH = 8

Ports (all addresses index 2**WIDTH = 64 locations, so addresses are 6 bits wide):
- clk           input,  1 bit
- rst_n         input,  1 bit
- write_en      input,  1 bit
- write_addr    input,  [WIDTH-1:0]  (6 bits)
- write_data    input,  [WIDTH-1:0]  (6 bits)
- read_en       input,  1 bit
- read_addr     input,  [WIDTH-1:0]  (6 bits)
- read_data     output reg, [WIDTH-1:0] (6 bits)

Clocking/reset: fully sequential. Both always blocks are `posedge clk or negedge rst_n` — asynchronous, active-low reset.

Storage: one array of 2**WIDTH = 64 words, each WIDTH = 6 bits wide, driven by non-blocking assignments. (The spec's literal `reg [DEPTH-1:0] RAM [2**WIDTH-1:0]` conflicts with its own "each with a width of 6 bits" and with the 6-bit write_data; use WIDTH-wide words so the data ports match.)

Behaviour:
- Write block: on !rst_n, every one of the 64 locations is cleared to 6'b000000 (this is the "initialized to 000000" requirement); else if write_en, RAM[write_addr] <= write_data.
- Read block: on !rst_n, read_data <= 0; else if read_en, read_data <= RAM[read_addr]; else read_data <= 0. Read is registered, so read_data appears 1 clock after read_en/read_addr are sampled.
- Reads and writes proceed independently in the same cycle (dual port).

Boundary cases stated by the spec: read_en low forces read_data to 0 (not a hold); reset clears both the whole array and read_data. Same-address simultaneous read/write is not specified — with both blocks non-blocking, the read returns the pre-write value.

Module name: ROM

Ports:
- addr : input, 8 bits, [7:0]
- dout : output, 16 bits, [15:0]

Storage:
- Internal memory array: reg [15:0] mem [0:255] — 256 words × 16 bits.
- Preloaded in an `initial` block: mem[0]=16'hA0A0, mem[1]=16'hB1B1, mem[2]=16'hC2C2, mem[3]=16'hD3D3. Remaining 252 locations are unspecified by the description; initialize them to a defined value (e.g. 16'h0000) so reads outside 0–3 are not X.

Clock/reset:
- None. The spec states no clock and no reset.

Timing:
- Purely combinational. Read path is `always @(*)` with `dout` declared as reg [15:0]. Zero pipeline latency: dout tracks addr in the same delta cycle.

Behaviour:
- dout is continuously assigned the contents of mem at index addr; the module is read-only, so no write port, no enable, and no output register exist.

Boundary cases:
- The description calls out none. addr is 8 bits and the array is exactly 256 deep, so every address is in range and no out-of-range or wrap-around case can occur. No overflow, full/empty, or divide-by-zero conditions apply.

Module name: instr_reg

Ports (all directions/widths exact):
- input clk
- input rst
- input [1:0] fetch
- input [7:0] data
- output [2:0] ins
- output [4:0] ad1
- output [7:0] ad2

Clock/reset:
- Sequential logic on the rising edge of clk.
- rst is active low. The spec describes reset being sampled at the rising clock edge ("On the rising edge of the clock, if rst is low, both registers are initialized to zero"), so implement it as synchronous active-low reset in the same always block.

Structure:
- Two internal 8-bit registers: ins_p1, ins_p2. These are the only state; latency from data to outputs is one clock cycle.
- Outputs are purely combinational slices of the registers (continuous assignment), no extra pipeline stage.

Behaviour:
- On each rising clk: if rst==0, ins_p1 <= 8'b0 and ins_p2 <= 8'b0; else if fetch==2'b01, ins_p1 <= data; else if fetch==2'b10, ins_p2 <= data; otherwise both registers hold their previous values.
- ins = ins_p1[7:5] (high 3 bits, opcode), ad1 = ins_p1[4:0] (low 5 bits, register address), ad2 = ins_p2 (full 8 bits from the second source).

Boundary cases stated by the spec:
- fetch == 2'b00 and fetch == 2'b11: no register is loaded; both retain previous values.
- Only one register is written per cycle; the fetch encodings are mutually exclusive, with 2'b01 selecting ins_p1 and 2'b10 selecting ins_p2.
- Reset takes priority over any fetch value.
- No overflow, divide-by-zero, full/empty, or wrap-around conditions apply to this module.

Module name: `pe`

Ports:
- `clk` — input, 1 bit
- `rst` — input, 1 bit
- `a` — input, 32 bits, `[31:0]`
- `b` — input, 32 bits, `[31:0]`
- `c` — output reg, 32 bits, `[31:0]`

Clock/reset:
- Sequential; single always block sensitive to `posedge clk or posedge rst` (asynchronous, active-high reset as the spec explicitly states).
- `rst` high → `c` <= 32'b0.

Behaviour:
- On each rising clock edge with `rst` low, `c <= c + (a * b)`; `c` is the accumulator register itself and is driven directly as the output.
- The product `a * b` is truncated/wrapped to 32 bits, and the accumulation likewise wraps modulo 2^32 — the spec specifies a 32-bit output register and calls out no wider intermediate, no overflow flag, and no saturation.
- Combinational logic is only the multiply and add feeding the register; latency is 1 cycle from operand sampling to updated `c`.

Boundary cases named by the spec:
- Reset (async, active high) forces `c` to 0 — this is the only special case the description calls out. No overflow/saturation handling is specified.

Module: square_wave

Ports:
- clk — input, 1 bit
- freq — input, 8 bits, [7:0]
- wave_out — output (reg), 1 bit

Clocking/reset:
- All state updates on posedge clk.
- No reset port is specified; do not add one. Initialize count and wave_out to 0 via initial-value declaration.

Structure:
- Purely sequential; no combinational outputs, no pipeline latency requirement.

Internal state:
- count — reg [7:0], free-running counter of clocks between toggles.

Behaviour:
- On each posedge clk: if count == freq - 1, set count <= 0 and wave_out <= ~wave_out; otherwise count <= count + 1.
- Output half-period is freq clock cycles, so larger freq yields a slower square wave.

Boundary cases called out by the spec:
- None stated regarding freq == 0 or count/freq overflow; freq - 1 is computed in 8-bit arithmetic and wraps naturally (freq == 0 compares against 8'hFF). Do not add special-case handling beyond this.

Module name: pulse_detect

Ports (all 1-bit scalars):
- clk — input, 1 bit, clock
- rst_n — input, 1 bit, active-low asynchronous reset
- data_in — input, 1 bit
- data_out — output, 1 bit, registered

Clocking/reset:
- Sequential logic on posedge clk, with asynchronous active-low reset (always block sensitive to posedge clk or negedge rst_n).
- On reset: state returns to the initial state and data_out is driven to 0.

Behaviour:
- A registered state machine tracks the input history and detects the 3-cycle sequence data_in = 0 then 1 then 0. data_out is asserted to 1 during the cycle in which the final 0 of that sequence is observed, and is 0 in all other cycles.
- data_out is a registered output; it returns to 0 the cycle after assertion unless another completed pulse is detected.

Overlap / back-to-back rule required by the spec:
- The trailing 0 of one pulse also serves as the leading 0 of the next pulse. For data_in = 0,1,0,1,0 the output must be 0,0,1,0,1 — i.e. two detections in five cycles.

Boundary cases stated:
- Reset forces state to initial and data_out to 0.
- No overflow, divide-by-zero, or full/empty conditions apply.

Module name: serial2parallel

Ports:
- clk — input, 1 bit (rising edge active)
- rst_n — input, 1 bit (active-low reset)
- din_serial — input, 1 bit
- din_valid — input, 1 bit
- dout_parallel — output, 8 bits [7:0]
- dout_valid — output, 1 bit

Timing/structure:
- Fully synchronous; all state updates on posedge clk. Reset polarity is active low (spec states active-low; use it as the reset condition — either synchronous or asynchronous reset is acceptable, no async requirement is stated).
- Sequential (registered) outputs. No pipeline latency beyond the shift itself: dout_valid asserts in the same cycle the 8th bit lands in dout_parallel.

Internal state required by the spec:
- cnt — 4-bit counter tracking the number of valid serial bits received.

Behaviour:
- When din_valid is 1, shift din_serial into dout_parallel and increment cnt; bits arrive MSB-first, so the first bit of a group ends up in dout_parallel[7] and the eighth in dout_parallel[0].
- dout_valid is 1 exactly on the cycle where the 8th bit of a group has been captured (cnt reached 8 bits received), and 0 otherwise. When din_valid is 0, cnt and dout_parallel hold; no new bit is consumed.

Boundary cases stated by the spec:
- Reset (rst_n low): clear cnt, dout_parallel, and dout_valid.
- cnt wraps back to 0 after every 8th received bit so consecutive 8-bit groups are converted continuously.
- dout_valid must be 0 in every cycle that is not an 8th-bit completion cycle.

module alu — purely combinational, no clock, no reset.

Ports:
  input  [31:0] a
  input  [31:0] b
  input  [5:0]  aluc
  output [31:0] r
  output        zero
  output        carry
  output        negative
  output        overflow
  output        flag

Behaviour: a 33-bit internal result `res` is computed by a case on aluc; r = res[31:0] and carry = res[32]. ADD/SUB operate on signed a,b and set overflow on signed 32-bit overflow; ADDU/SUBU are unsigned and produce carry/borrow in res[32]. AND/OR/XOR/NOR are bitwise. SLT compares a,b as signed, SLTU as unsigned. SLL/SRL/SRA shift b by a (SRA arithmetic); SLLV/SRLV/SRAV shift b by a[4:0]. LUI gives {a[15:0], 16'b0} (upper 16 bits of the result come from a's low half per the concatenation described).

Flags: zero = (r == 32'b0); negative = r[31]; overflow asserted only for signed ADD/SUB; carry is res[32]. flag = result of the comparison for SLT/SLTU (1 when a < b), and 1'bz for every other aluc value.

Boundary cases the spec calls out:
  - signed overflow on ADD and SUB only (ADDU/SUBU do not flag overflow)
  - carry-out/borrow captured as the 33rd bit
  - undefined aluc: r driven to 32'bz
  - flag driven to 1'bz for all non-SLT/SLTU opcodes
  - shift amounts use only the low 5 bits for the variable-shift (V) forms

Module: signal_generator

Ports:
- clk — input, 1 bit — clock
- rst_n — input, 1 bit — active-low reset
- wave — output reg, 5 bits [4:0] — generated triangle waveform

Clocking/reset:
- Single always block sensitive to posedge clk or negedge rst_n (asynchronous, active-low reset).
- On ~rst_n: state <= 0, wave <= 0.

Internal state:
- state — 1-bit register (0 = counting up, 1 = counting down). Not a port.

Behaviour (sequential, no pipeline latency beyond the single register stage):
- Every clock, a case on state selects direction: state==0 → wave <= wave + 1; state==1 → wave <= wave - 1.
- Direction flips at the endpoints: while in state 0, reaching wave == 31 sets state <= 1; while in state 1, reaching wave == 0 sets state <= 0. Output wave is the register itself (combinationally driven straight to the port).

Boundary cases called out by the spec:
- wave must stay within 0..31; it must never wrap 31→0 or 0→31, so the turnaround comparison at 31 (up) and 0 (down) must take effect on the same edge that would otherwise overflow/underflow the 5-bit value.
- Reset asserted asynchronously at any time forces wave to 0 and direction to up.

Note: the spec states both "increment when state==0" and "transition to 1 when wave==31" in the same state without saying which the register takes that cycle; implement the turnaround so wave holds/steps back rather than overflowing, keeping the sequence bounded to 0..31.

Module: freq_divbyfrac

Ports:
- clk: input, 1 bit — source clock
- rst_n: input, 1 bit — active-low reset
- clk_div: output, 1 bit — fractionally divided clock (source / 3.5)

Parameter: MUL2_DIV_CLK = 7 (twice the division ratio 3.5)

Clocking/reset:
- Sequential; two register sets, one clocked on posedge clk, one on negedge clk.
- Reset is asynchronous, active low (rst_n), applied to both edge domains.

Behaviour:
- A counter running on posedge clk counts 0..MUL2_DIV_CLK-1 (0..6) and wraps to 0.
- From that counter an intermediate clock clk_div1 is produced with an uneven duty: high for 4 source cycles and low for 3 (period alternates 4/3 across the 7-cycle window).
- A second intermediate clk_div2 is the same waveform resampled on the negedge of clk, i.e. shifted by half a source clock period relative to clk_div1.
- clk_div = clk_div1 | clk_div2 (combinational OR of the two intermediates), which evens out the 4/3 imbalance so the output has a uniform 3.5-cycle period.

Latency: no pipeline requirement beyond the half-cycle offset between the two intermediate clocks.

Boundary cases stated by the spec:
- Counter wrap-around at MUL2_DIV_CLK-1 back to 0.
- Reset must initialize counter and both intermediate clock registers to a known state.
- Duty-cycle imbalance of the 4-cycle vs 3-cycle halves is corrected by the OR of the two half-period-offset clocks.

MODULE: radix2_div

PORTS
  input  clk                  1-bit   clock
  input  rst                  1-bit   reset
  input  sign                 1-bit   1 = signed division, 0 = unsigned
  input  [7:0] dividend       8-bit   dividend operand
  input  [7:0] divisor        8-bit   divisor operand
  input  opn_valid            1-bit   operation request valid
  output res_valid            1-bit   result valid / ready
  output [15:0] result        16-bit  {remainder[7:0], quotient[7:0]}

CLOCK/RESET: all state updates on posedge clk; rst is active-high and synchronous, clearing cnt, start_cnt, res_valid and the shift register.

TYPE/LATENCY: sequential, iterative (not combinational, not pipelined). One accept cycle latches operands and loads SR with |dividend|<<1, sets cnt=1/start_cnt=1; then 8 shift-subtract iterations, so result appears 9 clocks after acceptance. Only one operation in flight; new operands are accepted only while opn_valid=1 and res_valid=0.

BEHAVIOUR: Holds a 17-bit shift register SR = {partial_remainder, quotient_bits}. Each iteration adds NEG_DIVISOR (two's-complement negation of the absolute divisor) to the upper half; if the carry-out is 1 the subtraction result is kept, otherwise the original upper half is kept, and SR shifts left with carry-out inserted as the new quotient bit. When cnt reaches 8 (its MSB set), cnt and start_cnt clear and SR is updated with the final remainder and quotient. When sign=1 the operands are used as magnitudes and the final quotient is negated if dividend and divisor signs differ, while the remainder takes the sign of the dividend; when sign=0 operands are treated as unsigned and no negation occurs.

BOUNDARY CASES: res_valid asserts when the iteration count completes and stays high until the result is consumed (opn_valid deasserted), then clears; rst clears it immediately. No divide-by-zero or overflow behaviour is specified by the description, so none is added.
